name: Cases & Variants (OCEL)
author: István Koren
description: The object-centric analog of the traditional "Cases & variants" view. Cases become process executions (Adams, Schuster, Schmitz, Schuh & van der Aalst, "Defining Cases and Variants for Object-Centric Event Data", arXiv:2208.03235): connected subgraphs of the object co-occurrence graph, extracted either by connected components or by a chosen leading object type. Variants become equivalence classes of process executions under activity-labeled graph isomorphism (Weisfeiler-Lehman canonical hashing, then exact verification within each hash bucket). Create execution partition publishes the typed, source-bound memberships for downstream views without duplicating OCEL records.

extraction.title: Extraction method
extraction.description: Leading type: each object of the chosen type roots its own process execution (closest related objects are pulled in). Connected components: every transitively co-occurring object is grouped into one execution — parameter-free, but can produce a few very large executions on a highly entangled log.

leadingType.title: Leading object type
leadingType.description: Only used when extraction is Leading type. The most frequent object type is selected automatically for a new view.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT object_type AS value, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {object} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: Trims the variant list to the top variants whose cumulative share of process executions reaches this percentage.

maxEvents.title: Max events per execution
maxEvents.description: On a densely entangled object graph (a shared hub object — an employee, a truck, a busy customer — links a large part of the log together), a single execution's true event set can approach the whole log. Executions are truncated to their chronologically-first N events past this limit — still a real, comparable graph, just a partial one — to keep extraction from taking minutes. Raise it to see more of each large execution, at the cost of a slower extraction.

scopeSharedObjects.title: Scope shared objects to their closest case
scopeSharedObjects.description: Only used when extraction is Leading type. A resource reused across many cases (a runway, a fuel truck) is still included in every case it touches, but only its events closest to that specific case are counted — its other, unrelated appearances elsewhere in the log are not. This is a deliberate deviation from the paper's Definition 4 (which includes an object's entire event history wherever the object appears); turn it off to see the paper's strict reading instead.

chevronColor.title: Color chevrons...
chevronColor.description: By involved object types (default): each chevron is split into diagonal bands, one per distinct object type touching that event — Table I's own convention for a shared event ('colored with the corresponding colors'), and ocpa's rendering — with each lane also getting a pale wash of its own type behind the whole row, same as 'by swimlane', so a lane's own type still reads at a glance. By activity: every chevron is a single solid color from its activity, like the Variants/Cases path chips and the rest of the view — the same activity reads as the same color in every lane, at the cost of not showing which object types share the event (no lane wash either, since a lane's type plays no part in this mode). By swimlane: every chevron in a lane takes that lane's own object-type color (plus the pale row wash) — good for visually tracking which single object type dominates an execution, but blind to any other type sharing the event.
